subject: gunblade
pitch:
Category: Weapon.
Subject: gunblade.
Style: Final Fantasy.
reasoning:
I'm thinking through how to position a Final Fantasy-style gunblade model as a static object standing upright on the ground, deciding whether the pommel or blade tip should touch the floor at y=0.

For construction, I'm planning to build it without joints since it's a static piece, using extruded geometry for the blade with its broad face oriented toward the viewer. I'm sketching out the components: a wrapped-leather grip cylinder at the base, a pommel, and above that a revolver-style cylinder, trigger guard, and hammer where the blade begins, keeping the whole thing vertical for simplicity.

I'm working out how the gunblade's receiver and cylinder fit together—placing a steel receiver block above the grip, adding a drum cylinder with its axis running parallel to the blade length rather than crosswise, and giving it six small chamber circles on top. Then I'm detailing the blade itself with a fuller groove, a thickened spine housing a barrel, and figuring out which side the edge and trigger should sit on relative to the grip.

I'm deciding to put the trigger toward the edge side and the hammer at the back of the grip, then adding a lion-head pendant emblem on the guard instead of a full chain, plus gilt trim and a glowing rune texture along the fuller to give it that magical blade feel. I'm planning to keep the code concise but detailed, using flat steel/gilt/blued/leather materials pulled from a clockwork kit along with a glow texture for the rune.

Now I'm sketching out the blade's outline geometry, mapping coordinates across and up from the base.

Still writing geometry...

Adding spine rivets...

Then I'm adding a glowing rune fuller down the blade center — thin planes on both faces with a rune texture, facing outward on each side.

Now I'm placing the receiver box around the base of the blade, with a revolver-style drum cylinder nestled beside it, giving the drum blued metal with gilt bands and flutes, and brass bullet-case heads along its rim.

Below that I'm shaping the trigger guard as a torus arc rotated into the lower half-circle beneath the receiver, plus a small curved trigger rod extending down from its center, and I'm starting on the hammer piece next.

Now I'm building the grip: a leather cylinder from y .04 to .30 wrapped with dark leather stripes and gilt bands at each end, then a gilt lathe-dome pommel sitting flush on the floor with a small flat base for stability. I'm also planning a lion pendant hanging from the pommel via a closed, swept gilt chain loop, making sure it stays above the ground plane.

Instead of chaining to the guard, I'll skip that and add a lion emblem decal onto the guard's front face, plus a matching emblem plate on the receiver front -- designing a simple gold circle-and-mane lion icon with eyes and face details. I'm also sketching glowing white-cyan rune glyphs for texture overlays, and extending the spine/barrel geometry up to its tip near y 1.2.

Now I'm detailing the muzzle cap with a dark cylinder ring and circle cap, adding a gilt ricasso collar at the blade base, and placing three cyan-glowing gem spheres on the guard's center front.

Setting up the part-building helper functions for boxes and cylinders, then positioning the drum ring cylinders in a circular pattern and shaping the trigger guard as a rotated torus arc dipping below the grip.

Continuing the hammer rod and adding a small box, then placing the receiver box above it, sizing the drum cylinder to overlay as the visual receiver, and shrinking the actual receiver box so it sits just below the drum. I'm deciding to skip extra ornamental wing plates and finalize the geometry for writing.
